title: Swatch Internet Time Clock
intro: Swatch Internet Time expresses the same worldwide instant as a number of beats, independent of the observer's time zone.
structure: The reference day begins at 00:00 on a fixed UTC+01:00 offset (Biel reference time). It is divided into 1000 beats; one beat lasts 86.4 ordinary seconds. Readings are @000 through @999; the optional fractional display has hundredths of a beat, each lasting 0.864 seconds.
example: At 23:00 UTC the reference day starts at @000. At 11:00 UTC, reference noon, the reading is @500. At 17:00 UTC it is @750. With fractional precision the noon reading is @500.00.
history: This is the modern Swatch Internet Time convention, intended as a time-zone-independent notation. The fixed reference offset is not the seasonal local civil time in Switzerland.
model: The provider adds a fixed 3600 seconds to the UTC day phase, takes positive modulo one day, then floors the phase scaled by either 1000 or 100000 ticks per day. It formats a three-digit beat count, optionally followed by two fractional digits, and schedules the next boundary with upward millisecond rounding.
limits: The caller's local offset, geographic coordinates and vertical display flag do not alter this notation. It does not observe daylight-saving adjustments to the reference offset and is not a local wall-clock display.
